chunks: From him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Ribat, and al-Husayn ibn Hashim and Safwan, all from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The emancipation of the intoxicated person is not valid."

key_terms.عِتْقُ: Emancipation or freeing of a slave

ai.seo_question: Is the emancipation of an intoxicated slave valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes that the emancipation ('itq) of a slave by an intoxicated master is legally invalid, drawing a parallel to the general principle that intoxication nullifies legal capacity (ahliyyah) in Shia jurisprudence. Scholars utilize this ruling to demonstrate that the mental clarity required for valid transactions is absent during drunkenness, thereby rendering the act of freeing the slave void rather than merely suspended.
